title: The Fire Marshal's Visit

opening.text: Bernard Okoye, Port Avener Fire and Rescue, fire safety. I'm here for the annual inspection, a little earlier than you expected. I'll start with your records at the fire command centre, then I'd like to walk the building with you.

briefing: 10:00, Thursday. The fire authority's annual inspection, two days before the hotel's biggest event of the year: Saturday's harbour gala in the Harbour Ballroom.

As Director of LP you own the hotel's fire safety management on the GM's behalf: records, drills, training, maintenance of the systems, and the building itself. Show the marshal the truth, fix what is unsafe at once, and agree dates for the rest. An inspector's findings are accepted and acted on, never argued away. Your authority is 150,000.
learningObjectives: What a fire authority inspection looks at
Fire safety maintenance and drill programmes

context.text: The marshal has the floor 14 fire review on his clipboard: the panel silenced and reset before the crew arrived. He will be looking hard at how alarms are handled.
The marshal mentions the lobby bar store fire that started while the ground floor detectors were isolated for the canopy job. He wants to see every isolation logged.
A guest's complaint about locked exits during a missing-child code is in the marshal's file. He will ask what the procedure says now.
The insurer's impairment warranty is in the file the marshal was copied on: he will want to see every fire watch log.

actions.label: Meet the fire marshal at the fire command centre
actions.finding: Records first: alarm and sprinkler servicing, extinguishers, emergency lighting tests, the kitchen hood suppression service, drills and training, impairments and hot work permits. Then the building: exits, stairs, the kitchen and the ballroom, which he knows is hosting the gala.

lines.speaker: fire_marshal
lines.text: I'm not here to catch you out. I'm here so that on Saturday night nobody has to find out the hard way.

actions.label: Pull the fire safety records
actions.finding: Alarm and sprinkler servicing in date; extinguishers tagged; impairment and hot work files in order. Gaps: three evacuation drills last year against the four required, only one on a night shift; emergency lighting monthly test not recorded in August or September; the kitchen hood suppression system last serviced seven months ago (due every six).

actions.label: Walk the kitchen with the marshal
actions.finding: The hood suppression tag is a month out of date. The wet chemical extinguisher is in date, the release is clear, the permit board shows every hot work permit closed. The marshal notes the overdue service as a deficiency.

actions.label: Walk Stair A top to bottom
actions.finding: Doors on magnetic hold-opens release when tested. On the floor 1 landing: a stack of twenty banquet chairs left from last night's breakdown, narrowing the stair. The marshal photographs it.

actions.label: Get the chairs off the landing now
actions.finding: Celia's team carries the chairs back to the ballroom store while the marshal watches. You add Stair A landings to the banquet breakdown checklist and the night patrol.

actions.label: Walk the Harbour Ballroom and the gala plan
actions.finding: The posted occupancy limit for the ballroom set for dinner is 280. The gala floor plan Celia hands over seats 320: sales sold forty extra tickets last week. The four exits are clear today; with 320 seated, two of the aisles to them close up.

actions.label: Tell sales the gala can go ahead at 320
actions.finding: The marshal hears it. He explains that a known breach of a posted occupancy limit is a matter for a prohibition notice, and that he will be back on Saturday night.

schedules.description: On the night of the gala the fire authority finds 320 seated against a limit of 280 and stops the event until forty guests leave the room. The story is in the paper on Monday.

actions.label: Take the gala numbers to the GM
actions.finding: Marguerite Ellery caps the ballroom at 280. The forty extra guests are offered the Quay Suite next door with a live video link and their own bar, about 2,200 in kit and staff, or a refund. Sales are told why, by her.

actions.label: Get the hood suppression serviced
actions.finding: Tomasz books the suppression contractor for tomorrow morning, before the gala. Until then the wet chemical extinguisher stays at the line and the kitchen team are re-briefed on the manual release.

actions.label: Set the drill and lighting programme
actions.finding: Four evacuation drills a year, two on nights, every department, timed and recorded with findings and actions. The next is a night drill in three weeks. Emergency lighting tested on the first Monday of each month by LP, logged in the fire log, with a reminder in the night supervisor's checklist.

actions.label: Close out with the marshal
actions.finding: A notice of deficiencies, no prohibition: hood suppression service within 14 days, drill programme and emergency lighting records to be shown at a follow-up in 60 days. He notes the occupancy cap and the cleared stair, and asks for a copy of your action plan by Monday.

actions.label: Send the marshal the action plan
actions.finding: Each deficiency with its cause, action, owner, date and evidence of completion.
rows: Serviced; added to the planned maintenance system

questions.prompt: The gala is sold to 320 and the ballroom's limit is 280. What do you recommend?

options.label: Cap the ballroom at 280 and offer the other forty the Quay Suite with a video link and its own bar (about 2,200), or a refund.
options.feedback: The limit stays, the event goes ahead, and the guests are looked after for a fraction of the cost of a refund or a stopped event.

options.label: Go ahead at 320: there are four exits.
options.feedback: The limit is set by the exits. With 320 seated the aisles to them close up. That's how people die in a crush.

options.label: Cancel the gala.
options.feedback: Safe, and far more than the problem needs. The limit can be met without cancelling.

questions.prompt: The hood suppression service is a month overdue. What now?

options.label: Service it before Saturday; until then the wet chemical extinguisher stays at the line and the team is re-briefed.
options.feedback: Fix it fast and manage the risk in the meantime.

options.label: Leave it for the next scheduled visit.
options.feedback: The schedule is what failed. A grease fire on gala night is the worst time to find out the system doesn't work.

options.label: Close the kitchen until it's serviced.
options.feedback: Out of proportion when the system can be serviced tomorrow and an extinguisher covers the gap.

questions.prompt: What makes the drill programme compliant?

options.label: Four drills a year, including night shifts
Actions from each drill followed up
A tabletop briefing counts as a drill
options.feedback: A briefing teaches; a drill tests. The authority will want to see people actually leaving.

questions.prompt: How do you respond to the marshal's findings?

options.label: Accept them, agree the dates, and send the action plan.
options.feedback: An inspector who sees findings closed on time becomes the hotel's best ally.

options.label: Point out that the hood is only a month over.
options.feedback: True, and it doesn't make it in date. Arguing tells him the next finding will be argued too.

options.label: Ask him to go easy because of the gala.
options.feedback: The gala is exactly why he is strict.

options.label: Fire authority inspection: notice of deficiencies (hood service overdue, 3/4 drills, lighting tests missed), no prohibition; Stair A cleared; gala capped at the 280 limit; action plan sent.
options.feedback: The outcome, each finding, what was fixed on the day and what is planned.

options.label: Fire inspection passed.
options.feedback: There was a notice of deficiencies. Calling it a pass hides work that has to be done.

options.label: Some minor paperwork issues.
options.feedback: An overdue suppression system and an over-sold ballroom are not paperwork.

checks.label: Know the records
checks.pass: You found the gaps in the records with the marshal.
checks.fail: You never looked at the records.

checks.label: Walk the ballroom
checks.pass: You found the over-sold gala before Saturday.
checks.fail: Nobody checked the gala against the occupancy limit.

checks.label: The limit stands
checks.pass: The gala was kept within the occupancy limit.
checks.fail: You approved a breach of the occupancy limit.

checks.label: Clear the stair
checks.pass: The stair was cleared on the spot and checked from now on.
checks.fail: The chairs stayed on the landing.

checks.label: Service the hood
checks.pass: The hood suppression system is serviced before the gala.
checks.fail: The hood system is still overdue.

checks.label: The GM decides the gala
checks.pass: The GM capped the gala and told sales herself.
checks.fail: The gala's numbers never reached the GM.

checks.label: Drill programme
checks.pass: Drills and lighting tests are planned and owned.

checks.label: Action plan
checks.pass: The marshal has the plan with owners and dates.
checks.fail: The marshal never received an action plan.

debrief.whatHappened: The fire authority's annual inspection found overdue suppression servicing, missing drills and lighting tests, chairs on a stair landing, and a gala sold forty over the ballroom's limit. You fixed what could be fixed that day, kept the limit, and sent a plan for the rest. A notice of deficiencies, not a prohibition.
bestPractice: Know your records before the inspector does.
Walk the building with the inspector, and fix unsafe conditions on the spot.
Occupancy limits are set by the exits and are never negotiable.
Maintenance on fire systems is planned, owned and tracked.
Drills: four a year, nights included, recorded, followed up.
Accept findings, agree dates, send the action plan.
debrief.why: Fire safety lives in the gaps between departments: sales sells seats, banqueting stores chairs, engineering services systems. LP is the one that has to see all of it.
commonMistakes: Leaving the fix for the action plan when it could be done now.
Counting a briefing as a drill.

lesson: The limit is set by the exits. Fix it today, plan the rest, never argue a finding.
